correctness.rationale: A positive definite regularized Laplacian has an injective linear edge-conductance map and a strictly convex trace inverse, proving a unique global optimum including boundary supports. Resistance identities of a weighted complete-graph block and the hub series law yield K_i=(N-q_i)/a_i+N(q_i-1)/(a_i+q_i b_i). Fixing a block budget reduces optimization to F(y)=(1-beta+beta*y)(A+B/y) for y>=1; an exact first derivative yields the unique shape optimum and universal ratio threshold 2N/(N-1), all price boundary cases included. Cauchy--Schwarz gives unique block budgets p_i=sqrt(C_i)/sum sqrt(C_j). Exact-rational independent Laplacian calculations and standard-library comparisons supplement, not replace, this universal analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The compared literature establishes general convex resistance design and fixed-weight windmill formulas, but none of the inspected material entails the derived all-petal price threshold, explicit optimal conductances, and global unique budget allocation. Full-text comparison performed for the two closest accessible original research papers; the inaccessible specialized windmill paper remains a declared genuine residual risk. Publication searches and published-finding corpus search are negative evidence only, not proofs of novelty.
residual_risks: The 2025 specialized windmill Kirchhoff paper was not available in full; its complete theorem statements could not be checked.
A differently named historic one-cut-vertex optimization theorem may imply the exact result despite alias searches.
A July 2006 conference precursor of the 2008 general paper exists, but its exact first-public calendar day was not established.

value.rationale: Clique bouquets model multiple densely connected local clusters reaching one shared hub, so deciding when costlier intracluster redundancy is worth buying is a natural resistive-network budget problem. The identical price cutoff for all differently sized petals at fixed total N is structurally nonobvious, and the theorem supplies exact unique conductances and the globally optimal objective for an infinite multi-parameter graph family. It avoids mere recomputation of unoptimized Kirchhoff index tables.
